classification.difficultyReason: Select subtraction of two stated excess amounts, recognise the remaining equal shares and halve the result in an unguided word problem.

content.prompt: At an election, there are three candidates, A, B and C. Candidate A obtains 19 878 more votes than C, and B obtains 12 435 more votes than C. Candidates A and B together obtain 137 187 votes. How many voted for C?

answer.short:
52 437 votes.

Subtract both excess vote counts from the combined total, then halve the remainder.
answer.worked:
Removing the extra votes from A and B leaves two equal shares, each equal to C’s votes.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Two equal shares}&=137\,187-19\,878-12\,435\\\text{Two equal shares}&=104\,874\\\text{Votes for C}&=104\,874\div2\\\text{Votes for C}&=52\,437\end{align*}$$
